facts.text: Rochester, Ohio takes its name from Rochester, New York, the hometown of a land agent who helped settle the area.
The Olmsted County Historical Society’s 100‑year exhibit celebrates a century of the History Center, spotlighting key people and buildings.
Visitors can explore how wartime conflicts shaped the community in the History Center’s “War Stories of Olmsted County” exhibit.
Today the History Center is restoring the Stoppel Farmstead, a historic property it owns, to preserve the story for future generations.
A new exhibit opened in November 2025 dives into the secret society of the Independent Order of Odd Fellows, active in Rochester from 1863 to 1999.
The Olmsted County Exhibit takes guests on a journey from prehistoric cephalopods and woolly mammoths to the present, covering Native peoples, early settlers, and surveying.
